lessons.title: Shawarma and Doner: Marination and Cooking
lessons.body:
Shawarma and doner are stacked meat cones cooked on a vertical rotisserie. In Africa, you can use beef, chicken, or lamb. Start with 2 kg of boneless chicken thighs or beef sirloin. For the marinade: blend 1 cup plain yogurt, 4 cloves garlic, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp ground cumin, 1 tbsp ground coriander, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Cut meat into thin strips or leave whole for stacking. Marinate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight in a fridge.

To cook without a rotisserie, use a heavy skillet or grill. For chicken thighs, cook on medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 75Â°C (165Â°F). For beef, cook to 60Â°C (140Â°F) for medium. Slice thinly against the grain. If you have a rotisserie, stack marinated meat on a skewer, pressing firmly. Cook on high heat for 20-30 minutes, turning, until the outside is crispy. Then slice off the outer layer, and continue cooking the inside.

For doner, you can also make a meatloaf-style block: mix 1 kg ground beef with 1 grated onion, 2 tbsp breadcrumbs, 1 egg, and the same spices. Shape into a log, bake at 200Â°C for 40 minutes, then slice and fry for crispness. This is cheaper and easier for street vending.

Serve in pita bread with tahini sauce, pickles, tomatoes, and onions. In Africa, use local spices like suya pepper or berbere for a twist. Keep meat hot in a cooler box or insulated container. For takeaway, wrap in foil or paper. Always cook to safe temperatures and keep raw meat separate from cooked. Clean your grill after each use to prevent sticking.

lessons.title: Falafel and Hummus from Scratch
lessons.body:
Falafel and hummus are made from chickpeas (garbanzo beans). For falafel, use dried chickpeas, not canned. Soak 2 cups dried chickpeas in water overnight (at least 12 hours). They will double in size. Drain well. In a food processor, blend chickpeas with 1 onion, 4 garlic cloves, 1 cup fresh parsley, 1 cup fresh cilantro, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, and 1 tbsp flour. Pulse until a coarse paste formsâdo not over-blend, or it becomes mushy. Chill for 30 minutes.

Shape into small balls (about 2 tbsp each). Heat oil to 175Â°C (350Â°F) in a deep pot. Fry in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown. Drain on paper towels. For a healthier version, bake at 200Â°C for 20 minutes, turning once. Falafel is best served hot in pita with tahini, pickles, and tomatoes.

For hummus, use canned chickpeas for speed. Drain and rinse 2 cans (400g each). In a blender, combine chickpeas, 1/2 cup tahini, 1/4 cup lemon juice, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp cumin. Blend, adding 1/4 cup ice water slowly until smooth and creamy. Adjust lemon and salt. Drizzle with olive oil and paprika. Hummus keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

In Africa, chickpeas are grown in Ethiopia, Sudan, and Kenya. Buy dried chickpeas from local marketsâthey are cheaper. For street vending, make falafel fresh daily. Serve hummus as a dip or spread. Use a food processor or heavy mortar and pestle if no electricity. Always taste and adjust seasoning. Fry falafel in clean oil; discard after 3-4 uses.

lessons.title: Pita Bread and Flatbreads
lessons.body:
Pita bread is a simple flatbread that puffs up in the oven. You need 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup warm water (about 40Â°C), 2 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp olive oil. Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add water and oil. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let rise for 1 hour, until doubled.

Punch down and divide into 8 balls. Roll each into a circle about 6 inches (15 cm) wide and 1/4 inch thick. Let rest for 15 minutes. Preheat oven to 250Â°C (480Â°F) with a baking stone or inverted baking sheet inside. Place 2-3 pita rounds on the hot surface. Bake for 3-4 minutes until they puff up and are lightly browned. Do not open the oven during baking. Remove and cover with a towel to keep soft.

If you don't have an oven, cook on a dry skillet or tawa on high heat. Cook each side for 1-2 minutes until bubbles form and brown spots appear. The bread will not puff as much but still tastes good. For flatbreads like khubz or taboon, you can add 1/2 cup yogurt to the dough for softness.

In Africa, use local flours like cassava or maize blended with wheat for a twist. For street vending, make pita fresh daily. Store in a plastic bag for 2 days, or freeze for 1 month. Reheat in a dry pan. Serve with shawarma, falafel, or as a wrap. Cut into triangles for dipping in hummus. Always keep dough covered to prevent drying. Adjust water if dough is too stickyâadd flour 1 tbsp at a time.

lessons.title: Mezze and Salads: Tabbouleh, Baba Ganoush
lessons.body:
Mezze are small dishes served together. Tabbouleh is a parsley salad. Use 1 cup fine bulgur (cracked wheat), soaked in 1 cup hot water for 20 minutes. Drain well. Chop 2 bunches parsley (about 4 cups), 1/2 cup mint, 4 tomatoes, 1 cucumber, and 1 small onion. Mix with bulgur. Dressing: 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper. Toss and chill. Tabbouleh should be green and fresh, not soggy. In Africa, use local parsley and mintâthey are cheap and abundant.

Baba ganoush is smoky eggplant dip. Roast 2 large eggplants (about 1 kg) directly over a gas flame or on a grill until skin is charred and flesh is soft, about 15-20 minutes. Alternatively, bake at 200Â°C for 40 minutes, then broil for 5 minutes to char. Cool, peel, and scoop flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork. Add 1/4 cup tahini, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 garlic cloves (minced), 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp cumin. Mix well. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika. Serve with pita.

For takeaway, pack tabbouleh in small containers and baba ganoush in tubs. Keep cold. These dishes are vegetarian and vegan, appealing to many customers. In Africa, eggplants are available in most markets. You can also add roasted red peppers or pomegranate seeds for color. Make small batches daily for freshness. Use clean utensils and gloves. Tabbouleh can be made ahead but add tomatoes just before serving to prevent sogginess. Baba ganoush lasts 3 days in fridge.

lessons.title: Wraps and Platters for Take Away
lessons.body:
Wraps and platters are the main way to sell Middle Eastern street food. A wrap is a pita or flatbread filled with meat, falafel, vegetables, and sauce. A platter is a plate with the same ingredients but no bread, often with rice or salad. For takeaway, use sturdy containers and wrap tightly.

To assemble a wrap: warm a pita for 10 seconds. Lay it flat. Spread 2 tbsp tahini or hummus. Add 100g sliced shawarma or 3 falafel balls. Top with 2 tbsp chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp pickles, 1 tbsp onions, and 1 tbsp parsley. Roll tightly, tucking in the sides. Wrap in foil or paper. For platters: use a compartment container. Put 150g meat or falafel, 1/2 cup rice or tabbouleh, 2 tbsp hummus, 2 tbsp salad, and 2 tbsp sauce. Include a piece of pita on the side.

In Africa, use local ingredients: rice, chapati, or ugali instead of pita. Add suya spice or piri piri for heat. For vegetarians, use extra falafel or grilled vegetables. Keep hot foods above 60Â°C and cold foods below 5Â°C. Use insulated bags for delivery. Label containers with contents and date.

For efficient service, set up an assembly line: one person warms bread, one adds fillings, one wraps. Use gloves and clean surfaces. Pre-portion sauces in small cups. For platters, use biodegradable containers if possible. Price wraps affordablyâthey are a complete meal. Offer combos: wrap + drink + fries. In busy areas, pre-wrap some and keep in a warmer. Always check for allergiesâtahini contains sesame. Provide napkins and a small bag. This is a high-turnover business; keep it simple and fast.

lessons.title: Sauces: Tahini, Amba, and Zhoug
lessons.body:
Sauces make Middle Eastern food special. Tahini sauce is creamy and nutty. Mix 1/2 cup tahini (sesame paste) with 1/4 cup lemon juice, 1 garlic clove (minced), 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 cup cold water. Whisk until smooth. It will seize first, then become creamy. Add more water for thinner consistency. Tahini sauce is used on falafel, shawarma, and salads. In Africa, you can make tahini by blending roasted sesame seeds with oil until smooth. Store in fridge for 2 weeks.

Amba is a pickled mango sauce, popular in Israel and Middle East. Use 2 ripe mangoes, peeled and chopped. In a pot, combine mangoes, 1/2 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp chili flakes, and 2 cloves garlic. Simmer for 20 minutes until soft. Blend until smooth. Cool and store in jars. Amba is tangy and spicy, great on shawarma or falafel. In Africa, use local mangoesâthey are abundant in season. You can also use green mangoes for more tang.

Zhoug is a spicy green sauce from Yemen. Blend 2 cups fresh cilantro, 1 cup parsley, 4 green chilies, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp cardamom, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/2 cup olive oil. Pulse until combined but not pureed. Store in fridge for 1 week. Zhoug is very hotâuse sparingly. It adds a kick to wraps and platters.

For street vending, make sauces in bulk and portion into squeeze bottles or small cups. Label them. Always keep cold. Tahini is vegan and gluten-free. Amba is sweet and spicy. Zhoug is for heat lovers. Offer all three so customers can choose. In Africa, adjust chili to local taste. Use clean spoons to avoid contamination. These sauces increase profit marginsâthey cost little but add value.

quiz.q: What is the best cut of meat for shawarma?
quiz.explanation: Shawarma can be made with beef, chicken, or lamb, so all are correct.

quiz.q: How long should you marinate meat for shawarma?
quiz.explanation: Marinating for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, allows flavors to penetrate.

quiz.q: What internal temperature should chicken reach for shawarma?
quiz.explanation: Chicken must be cooked to 75Â°C (165Â°F) to be safe.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is essential for falafel?
quiz.explanation: Falafel requires dried chickpeas soaked overnight, not canned, for proper texture.

quiz.q: What oil temperature is best for frying falafel?
quiz.explanation: 175Â°C (350Â°F) fries falafel evenly without burning.

quiz.q: What makes hummus creamy?
quiz.explanation: Ice water helps create a smooth, creamy texture in hummus.

quiz.q: How long can hummus be stored in the fridge?
quiz.explanation: Hummus keeps for about 4 days in the refrigerator.

quiz.q: What is the main flour used in pita bread?
quiz.explanation: Pita bread is typically made with all-purpose wheat flour.

quiz.q: At what temperature do you bake pita bread?
quiz.explanation: Pita bakes at a high temperature of 250Â°C (480Â°F) to puff up.

quiz.q: What can you use if you don't have an oven for pita?
quiz.explanation: A dry skillet or tawa on high heat can cook pita bread.

quiz.q: What grain is used in tabbouleh?
quiz.explanation: Tabbouleh is made with fine bulgur (cracked wheat).

quiz.q: How do you get the smoky flavor in baba ganoush?
quiz.explanation: Roasting eggplant directly over a flame chars the skin and gives a smoky flavor.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is NOT in traditional baba ganoush?
quiz.explanation: Traditional baba ganoush does not contain yogurt; it is vegan.

quiz.q: What is a common wrapper for Middle Eastern street food?
quiz.explanation: Pita, chapati, and even tortillas can be used as wraps.

quiz.q: What temperature should hot foods be kept at for takeaway?
quiz.explanation: Hot foods must be held above 60Â°C to prevent bacterial growth.

quiz.q: What is tahini made from?
quiz.explanation: Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds.

quiz.q: What fruit is used to make amba?
quiz.explanation: Amba is a pickled mango sauce.

quiz.q: Which sauce is known for being spicy and green?
quiz.explanation: Zhoug is a spicy green sauce made with cilantro and chilies.

quiz.q: How long can zhoug be stored in the fridge?
quiz.explanation: Zhoug keeps for about 1 week in the refrigerator.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for pita in African street food?
quiz.explanation: Ugali, chapati, and rice can all be used as alternatives to pita.

quiz.q: What should you do if tahini sauce seizes?
options: B) Add cold water and whisk
quiz.explanation: Adding cold water slowly while whisking will make it creamy again.

quiz.q: Which meat is traditionally used for doner kebab?
quiz.explanation: Doner can be made with beef, chicken, or lamb.

quiz.q: What is a key step before frying falafel?
quiz.explanation: Chilling the falafel mixture helps it hold together during frying.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient in hummus?
quiz.explanation: Hummus is primarily made from chickpeas.

quiz.q: How long should you soak dried chickpeas for falafel?
quiz.explanation: Dried chickpeas need at least 12 hours of soaking.

quiz.q: What is a common spice in shawarma marinade?
quiz.explanation: Shawarma marinade typically includes cumin, coriander, and paprika.

quiz.q: What is the best way to keep pita bread soft?
quiz.explanation: Covering freshly baked pita with a towel traps steam and keeps it soft.

quiz.q: Which of these is a mezze dish?
quiz.explanation: Tabbouleh, baba ganoush, and hummus are all part of a mezze spread.

quiz.q: What is a good vegan option for a wrap?
quiz.explanation: Falafel is a vegan-friendly filling for wraps.

quiz.q: What should you do with leftover frying oil?
quiz.explanation: Frying oil should be discarded after 3-4 uses to avoid off-flavors and health risks.
